memory_candidates.content: When parsing a unified git diff line-by-line, do NOT skip '---'/'+++'-shaped lines as file-header preamble based on shape alone -- a removed/added content line whose own text starts with '--' (e.g. a Lean/shell line comment) renders as '--- that comment' and is indistinguishable from a real '--- a/path' header by shape. Track whether the first '@@' hunk marker has been seen instead: only skip '---'/'+++'/'diff --git'/'index ' lines BEFORE that point; every line from the first '@@' onward is unambiguously +/-/context content, never a header. This matches how real diff tooling disambiguates the two cases.

check-extension-docs.sh's Rule E (check_referenced_scripts_declared) false-positives on an extension that legitimately references an EXTERNAL, non-agent-system script by name in its docs/skill/command (e.g. a consumer repository's own component script). Fixed by adding an optional manifest-level `external_scripts` array field, read as one more exclusion set parallel to the existing core_declared/all_declared_scripts/own_hooks sets -- backward-compatible (absent/empty for every other extension) and narrowly scoped to Rule E only. Any future extension needing to document an external script by name should declare it there rather than working around the lint.

orchestrator-context-budget.json's eager_load.baseline_bytes has a 5-entry history of closing every overage by trimming existing eager content, never by raising the baseline -- but that assumes the overage is always redistributable bloat. A brand-new extension's minimal CLAUDE.md-merged EXTENSION.md entry (heading + one sentence + a pointer) has an unavoidable floor cost of roughly 100+ bytes that cannot be trimmed away, since there is no pre-existing slack to redistribute for content that did not exist before. When the baseline's headroom is near zero (as it was here, ~9 B), adding ANY new command-providing extension will force a choice between a deliberate baseline move and omitting the extension's CLAUDE.md discoverability entry entirely.
